analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: Hotter-than-expected US inflation and still-high yields, more concentrated EM equity markets
key_insights: A hotter-than-expected US core CPI print pushed Treasury yields higher. European sovereign spreads remain wide partly on French and Italian fiscal concerns.
GS keeps a directional bias toward lower G4 sovereign yields but expects elevated long-term yields to have some staying power, with continued upside risk to yields from energy price pressures.

If yields stay near current levels, GS estimates a 0.5pp subtraction from US growth and 0.4-0.6pp from broader DM growth next year. Under the GS baseline, higher rates weigh on US GDP growth by about 0.2pp in 2027.
A further sharp rise in yields would pressure equities and corporate credit, especially if accompanied by higher rate volatility.

GS shifted to overweight bonds (from neutral) in its 12m asset allocation and to overweight equities (from neutral) in its 3m allocation. It cites continued strong earnings growth and lower equity valuations over the past several months. On net it favors equities over bonds in the near and medium term.
EM equity markets have become increasingly concentrated amid the AI investment boom. GS attributes this to exceptional profit growth rather than speculative exuberance.

For EM equities GS recommends diversifying across regions (selective opportunities in North Asia, India, LatAm and some CEE), balancing tech and momentum with defensive factors, considering alternate benchmarks (EM 10/40 and 25/50), and using derivative overlays to hedge risks.
US midterms: prediction markets have raised the odds of a Democratic sweep as voters focus on higher gasoline prices.

Brazil's presidential election goes to a second-round runoff on October 25. A market-friendly outcome conducive to a tighter fiscal stance could lead the Brazilian Real to appreciate further. GS lowered USD/BRL forecasts (3/6/12m) to 4.70/4.75/4.80 from 5.20/5.10/5.00.
In France, GS's poll-based model shows Marine Le Pen as the favorite to win next year's presidential election. GS thinks her fiscal proposal faces significant implementation challenges.

UK growth has accelerated this year, defying slowdown expectations. GS expects a slowdown over the winter on rising energy bills and higher mortgage rates, then improvement later in 2027 as gas prices likely fall and the BoE delivers less tightening than the market prices.
GS sees UK longer-run growth prospects brighter with closer UK-EU economic relations. The UK-EU summit is scheduled for November 20.
GS baseline forecasts: the Fed delivers one more hike in December, followed by three cuts starting in September 2027, and long-term rates ease from current levels in coming months.
